title: After noise complaints, judge orders Waymo to stop overnight charging in Santa Monica
gist: A Los Angeles Superior Court judge granted Santa Monica a preliminary injunction barring Waymo from operating its Broadway, 12th and Euclid Street charging lots between 11 pm and 6 am, on the theory that the vehicle noise and light constitute a public nuisance. Waymo has appealed; the underlying suit filed in November 2025, plus Waymo's counter-suit, returns to court in October 2026.

insights.claim: Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Bradley S. Phillips granted the City of Santa Monica a preliminary injunction barring Waymo from operating its charging lots on Broadway at 12th and Euclid Streets between 11 pm and 6 am.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Local nuisance law can now curtail autonomous-fleet depot hours, an operating constraint that does not appear in AV regulatory frameworks focused on driving safety.
insights.locator: A local judge has ruled that Waymo can no longer

insights.claim: The court accepted at the preliminary-injunction stage that a robotaxi charging depot may constitute a public nuisance because of light pollution, sound pollution and traffic congestion on surrounding streets and alleys.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Nuisance is a cheap, locally available cause of action — it gives any neighborhood a lever against AV infrastructure without waiting for state or federal rules.

insights.claim: The Broadway charging stations sit directly across the street from a private school and near apartment buildings, with residents complaining consistently for over a year before the ruling.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Siting charging depots in dense residential blocks is the underlying error — location diligence is now a material cost item for AV fleet expansion.
insights.locator: Under the new order, Waymo is forbidden

insights.claim: A resident living next to the lots testified that the constant reversing beep of the autonomous vehicles is an incessant disturbance affecting both daytime tranquillity and nighttime peace, making backup alarms rather than driving behavior the core complaint.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: The harm stems from mandated safety sounds and EV acceleration noise, meaning engineering fixes are constrained by other regulations.
insights.quote: The constant ‘beep beep beep’ sound as the autonomous vehicles back out of their spaces (in their own lots) is an incessant disturbance that hinders both our tranquillity during the day and our peace during the night,
insights.locator: wrote Christopher Potter, a man who says he lives right next to the lots

insights.claim: Peak disturbance ran at roughly 2 am when bars let out, when the lots operated at full volume, indicating depot activity tracks late-night ride demand precisely when residential noise tolerance is lowest.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: The most profitable robotaxi hours are the same hours a nuisance injunction shuts down — a direct hit to depot utilization economics.
insights.locator: Another neighbor, who wished to remain anonymous

insights.claim: Neighbors report an immediate, dramatic change in ambient noise since Waymo began complying with the overnight order, which strengthens the causal link the city must prove in the ongoing case.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Observable before-and-after relief is powerful evidence at the merits stage and raises the odds the injunction is made permanent.
insights.quote: You can hear the crickets, you can hear your thoughts, it’s not a fleet of locusts descending on the neighborhood, it’s incredible.
insights.locator: With the order in place, neighbors already notice a difference

insights.claim: Waymo began using the Santa Monica charging facilities in January 2025, the city ordered it to halt overnight operations after complaints and an online petition, and the city sued in November 2025; Waymo has counter-sued.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Roughly a year elapsed between depot opening and litigation — a repeatable escalation timeline for other cities hosting new AV infrastructure.
insights.locator: Waymo began using these charging facilities in January 2025

insights.claim: Waymo has appealed the injunction and did not immediately answer questions from Ars Technica, while the next hearing in the underlying case is set for October 2026.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: October 2026 is the date to watch for whether nighttime depot restrictions become a durable precedent in California.

insights.claim: Santa Monica Mayor Caroline Torosis publicly framed residents' ability to sleep as non-negotiable, signaling that city leadership is politically committed to the case rather than seeking a quiet settlement.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Elected officials campaigning on the dispute lowers the chance of a negotiated accommodation and raises regulatory risk for AV depot siting citywide.
insights.quote: Our residents’ ability to sleep peacefully in their own homes is not negotiable,
